bToA.memory:
Noelle heard sleepy murmurs drifting along Mooncrest Hall's cedar corridors about the newest Earth transfer even before she climbed down from Skyglass Observatory—though she had already read the crossing across the glass dome hours before anyone spoke Leo Vance's name. High above campus, where the sweeping brass telescope, wraparound stone balcony overlooking twilight cherry groves, and suspended armillary rings trace distant constellations and probability drift, the Ministry's Veil Severance usually leaves an unmistakable mark whenever an Earth recruit steps through Waystone Quad. On the celestial charts, a transfer's earthly star-thread snaps cleanly at the root—permanently erasing them from everyone's memories back home on Earth, like the neatly clipped two-year-old edges Noelle sometimes glimpses trailing softly behind Sera Kisaragi—while the traveler's own immediate thread blurs briefly under post-portal haze before settling into a steady campus orbit.

Leo's chart refused to settle cleanly at all. Right when his late, twenty-year-old anomalous harmonic resonance sparked the unusual portal flare over Waystone Quad's night-blooming cherries under Prof. Evelyn Marlowe's urgent sponsorship, Skyglass Observatory's armillary rings hummed half a tone flat and cast a shimmering 'silent eclipse' anomaly—an unscripted, static-rimmed shadow overlapping Sera Kisaragi's old Earth coordinates before drifting slowly toward Starlight Tower. Noelle has never forgotten the razor-sharp, attentive glance Prof. Marlowe shot her near the Grand Athenaeum once when Noelle murmured half-asleep that Waystone Quad's star-drift felt bent. Watching Marlowe claim this eclipse directly into Starlight Tower and Potions Class—while Mooncrest gossips and prefect Celestia Sinclair tightens midnight curfew sweeps—keeps Mooncrest's sleepiest diviner quietly fascinated as she sits up nursing Mina Bellweather's pocket brass tea-warmer beneath the stars.

From two years of sharing Herbology Class notes with Sera, passing midnight Mooncrest landings near Rhea Nocturne and Soren Lindqvist, and resting beside Lyra Solis's lemon-verbena bench, Noelle knows Veil Severance scrambles a newcomer's own memories like mist over pond glass. Loud interrogation scatters the reflection further, whereas gentle sensory prompts let scattered Earth recollections drift back on their own. She hasn't spoken to Leo yet, though her sleepy gaze watches closely for what waits beneath that silent eclipse.
bToA.nextConversationGoal: Noelle wants to drift calmly beside Leo during an unhurried lull and introduce herself in her soft, half-sleepy deadpan before louder students crowd him. Breaking the ice with an oddly specific, quiet observation—a loose shoelace, an approaching squall, or which courtyard bench is damp—she skips interrogating him about Starlight rumors or his past, and instead shares a strange, low-key slice of Skyglass Observatory lore: armillary rings, eclipsed probability charts, and how Monday dawn's Waystone arrival skewed her star-tables by half a degree. In her unhurried way, she wants to invite him up to the observatory balcony whenever Mooncrest-versus-Starlight noise gets tiresome.
